correctness.rationale: The deterministic total T_j=T_0+(a+b)j and exact difference recursion follow directly from the two replacement rules. The centered differences are bounded martingale increments with predictable variance v_N-(s lambda_N)^2(D_j/T_j)^2. The exact second-moment recursion bounds E[D_j^2] by C(j+1)(1+log(j+1)) uniformly over j<=N. Uniform gamma-product bounds reduce the log-clock process to a weighted martingale; its squared-proportion quadratic-variation correction is O(1/log N) in expectation, while the main weighted harmonic sum converges uniformly to v_* int_0^t exp(2 delta u) du. Bounded jumps give a functional martingale CLT, and gamma-ratio/Doob bounds supply uniform error control. The endpoint proportion factor is 1/[2(a+b)]. Running the packaged check.py verified 206 finite exact/algebraic/asymptotic assertions; these corroborate rather than prove the infinite limit. No claim is made for unequal or random total additions.

originality.rationale: The principal 2026 mixed-urn source proves a fixed-p, strictly diffusive terminal CLT, whose variance denominator tends to zero as p approaches the critical value; its conditions do not provide a uniform-in-p logarithmic-window theorem. The earlier fixed-p law of large numbers and fixed-matrix critical-urn martingale literature do not state the triangular array or nonzero-drift log-time OU interpolation. published-finding corpus searches for this source, near-critical eigenvalue, symmetric urns, and OU covariance found no implication covering this model. General randomized and nonhomogeneous urn theory creates a residual historical-priority risk, but abstract-level statements do not directly resolve the specific row-constant triangular-horizon process.
residual_risks: Older stochastic-approximation theorems could encompass varying eigenvalue triangular arrays without naming the mixed urn; there is no claim of definitive historical uniqueness.

Bai–Hu (1999) and Bai–Hu–Zhang (2002) full text could not be completely inspected; their abstract-level critical and nonhomogeneous assertions are not directly comparable enough to establish a dominating implication.

value.rationale: A fixed batch-size Friedman-versus-Pólya mixture is the natural balanced subclass of a newly studied random-replacement urn. The recent fixed-p theorem covers only a strict side of the spectral threshold, whose usual Gaussian variance diverges on approach. The parameter displacement theta/log N is the precise scale on which the eigenmode shift aggregates over logarithmic time, giving a nontrivial family of OU drifts rather than just another value of a fixed-parameter covariance. The theorem supplies all finite-dimensional covariances, the functional limit and an explicit terminal interpolation across both sides, while clearly separating its structural content from standard martingale-CLT machinery.
